The CBG is an active and engaged group dedicated to creating a stronger, more effective voice on business issues while also ensuring that each of our individual organizations remains empowered to serve its own members.
It is important to note that the CBG does not replace the role of any individual business association nor does it limit the actions of any group.
Instead, we work collaboratively on shared priorities, issues that impact businesses across industries, sectors and communities here in Saskatoon.
In February of 2007, a combined business group approached City Council at the time with a vision to renew and strengthen Saskatoon's commitment to being a business friendly city.
At the time, we asked Council to amend a 2002 resolution that recognized Saskatoon's position as one of Canada's best places to do business.
City Council at the time renewed its commitment and updated the resolution to read.
The city will continue to work to improve its position as the business friendly city in Canada.
Today, I stand before you on behalf of the combined business group to reflect on that great commitment of the past and to build upon it into the future.
We're asking City Council to declare, Saskatoon will be Canada's most business ready city in Canada.
What does that mean?
It means that Saskatoon will recognize nationally for its ease of doing business, competitive tax environment and strategic infrastructure investments.
It means that businesses big and small will choose Saskatoon because of supportive policies, collaborative leadership and strong economic outlook.
It means that when businesses succeed, our community thrives, creating jobs, fostering innovation and enhancing the quality of life for all residents.
It means businesses, employees and customers will feel safe and supported in Saskatoon.
Proactive policies and partnership that enhance public safety reduce crime and create secure commercial and industrial spaces.
The business ready Saskatoon pledge is a vision and we're presenting it to you today.
The principles presented to you and our letter are about ensuring long-term economic prosperity for Saskatoon.

The five guiding principles are treat local businesses as partners, streamline the business environment, reduce the cost of doing business, build transformational projects and infrastructure and enhance safety and security.
Today, I'm asking committee and City Council to formally endorse and adopt the business ready Saskatoon pledge as a framework for decision making over the next four years.
Public publicly reaffirm your commitment to making Saskatoon Canada's most business ready city.
Use these principles as a guide post for future decision making that impact businesses, economic development, and Saskatoon's reputation as a leading place to live work and invest.

Following this, I'll personally be reaching out to every individual and city council in your worship mayor block to individually request your signature on the pledge so that we can share this commitment with our memberships.
We are not here today to simply ask for support. We are here to partner with you to create a flourishing future for our city.
A business ready city is not just good for our businesses. It is the foundation of a thriving, prosperous community where workers, families and entrepreneurs can build their futures with confidence.
When businesses grow, we create opportunity, stability and conditions for long-term prosperity.
Being open for businesses about ensuring wealth and well-being for every resident, fostering innovation and strengthening the very fabric of our community.
This is how we all build the legacy. On behalf of the combined business group, I thank you for your time and consideration.
We look forward to working together to build the city that is vibrant, prosperous, and business ready. Thank you.
